body: Co-founder of Oaktree Capital (1995); memos since 1990 (the Jan 2000 'bubble.com' memo called the tech top); books The Most Important Thing (2011) and Mastering the Market Cycle (2018). Structural edge: a credit/distressed-debt franchise with locked-up capital that can deploy when others must sell. Signature trade: in 2008 Oaktree raised $10.9bn for OCM Opportunities Fund VIIb - its largest distressed fund, 3x the previous one - began investing in May 2008 and deployed most of it between Lehman's bankruptcy and year-end 2008 (reportedly ~$500m a week), targeting 25-30%+ gross; by 2011 it had returned $3bn to LPs (final realised IRR not found). Process: 'second-level thinking' (what is priced in, not just what is good); 'you can't predict, you can prepare' - take the market's temperature (credit spreads, issuance quality, investor attitudes, 'too good to be true' deals) and lean aggressive when fear is high and defensive when risk appetite is high; winning by avoiding losers. Mistakes: his cautious memos were early in several long bull runs (e.g., 2017-2021) - temperature reading gives direction, not timing. Copyable: build a simple 'market temperature' checklist for India (smallcap-to-Nifty P/E premium, IPO/SME subscription multiples, F&O retail volumes, market cap/GDP, credit spreads) and adjust equity allocation in steps rather than going all-in or all-out.

data.mistakes: early caution in long bull runs

title: Howard Marks - cycle positioning and second-level thinking
